claims.text: Covered services: Medicare Part B covers a PA's services only if, among other conditions, they would be covered if a physician furnished them and the PA is legally authorized to perform them in that state.
claims.quote: Medicare Part B covers physician assistants' services only if the following conditions are met: (1) The services would be covered as physicians' services if furnished by a physician (a doctor of medicine or osteopathy, as set forth in section 1861(r)(1) of the Act). (2) The physician assistant— (i) Meets the qualifications set forth in paragraph (c) of this section; (ii) Is legally authorized to perform the services in the State in which they are performed;

claims.text: State rules govern supervision: services must follow state law and scope-of-practice rules for PAs, including any supervisory or collaborative practice requirements.
claims.quote: Performs the services in accordance with state law and state scope of practice rules for physician assistants in the state in which the physician assistant's professional services are furnished. Any state laws and scope of practice rules that describe the required practice relationship between physicians and physician assistants, including explicit supervisory or collaborative practice requirements, describe a form of supervision

claims.text: Who bills: before January 1, 2022, a PA's services had to be billed by the PA's employer.
claims.quote: (v) Prior to January 1, 2022, furnishes services that are billed by the employer of a physician assistant

claims.text: 85% rate: Medicare pays a PA's services (other than assistant-at-surgery services) at 85% of the physician fee schedule amount.
claims.quote: (d) For services (other than assistant-at-surgery services) furnished beginning January 1, 1998, 85 percent of the physician fee schedule amount for the service.

claims.text: Incident-to: incident-to services must be an integral, though incidental, part of the physician's (or other practitioner's) service in diagnosing or treating an injury or illness.
claims.quote: (2) Services and supplies must be an integral, though incidental, part of the service of a physician (or other practitioner) in the course of diagnosis or treatment of an injury or illness.

claims.text: Incident-to supervision: in general, incident-to services must be furnished under the physician's (or other practitioner's) direct supervision.
claims.quote: (5) In general, services and supplies must be furnished under the direct supervision of the physician (or other practitioner).

notes.issue: Claim read the two conditions as sufficient; the regulation lists further conditions.
notes.resolution: Added 'only if, among other conditions'; re-check passed.
Added '(other than assistant-at-surgery services)'; re-check passed.
